scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! Our department is OFF THE NETWORK -- every
single one of our machines, all at once, can't reach anything!! Something
around the box all our wires go into must be wrong, but I don't know what.
Could someone look at it and get us back on the network -- the whole
department is sitting here doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough five-phase sweep of the Kath2 topology found no fault. Phase 1 (get_reachability) confirmed 0% loss for all sampled hosts. Phase A infrastructure sweep (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot) found no ACL drops, no missing IPs, no gateway divergence, and no real MAC conflicts — the "duplicate MACs" flagged by l2_snapshot are all zero-address entries on Linux kernel tunnel pseudo-interfaces (tunl0, gre0, etc.) that appear on every Linux host by default and carry no traffic. Phase B showed router0's RIP table with stable directly-connected routes to both the IT subnet (192.168.1.0/24 via eth0/switch0) and CS subnet (192.168.2.0/24 via eth1/switch1), plus learned routes to all other subnets; tc_snapshot showed default pfifo_fast on all 39 inspected interfaces with zero shaping. Direct probes to the most likely complainants — it_hod (192.168.1.2), it_lab1 (192.168.1.3), cs_hod (192.168.2.2), and enquiry (192.168.3.4) — each returned 0% packet loss to remote subnets. Phase D pressure_sweep found no stress tools, no CPU pressure, and no socket saturation on any of the 30 devices. There is no mechanism — no downed link, no flap script, no ACL rule, no routing black hole, no resource exhaustion — that could account for a whole-department outage. The complaint describes a symptom that is not reproducible in the current live state and leaves no historical trace.
Root cause: No fault present; topology is fully operational.
Fix: No corrective action required; monitor for recurrence and gather syslog/interface-counter snapshots if the issue reappears.
